figure_candidates.caption:
Fig. 1 | Tyrocidine synthetase and click crosslinking. a, Gene cluster (top) 
and modular organization of the tyrocidine A synthetase from B. parabrevis 
ATCC 8185. The biosynthetic gene cluster includes three NRPS genes (tycA, 
tycB and tycC) whose protein products (TycA, TycB and TycC, respectively) 
contain one (M1), three (M2–M4) and six (M5–M10) modules, respectively.  
The adenylation (A) domain in each module accepts and selectively loads one 
amino acid, as illustrated by l-Phe in M1 of TycA or l-Pro in M2 of TycB. Release 
from the synthetase by macrocylization is accomplished by the thioesterase 
(TE) domain. The structure of the condensation complex that unites the first 
two monomers is the focus of this study. b, Structure of the cyclic peptide 
tyrocidine A, depicting the position of the explored amide bond formation 
(purple) between d-Phe (green) on M1 to l-Pro (blue) on M2. c, Schematic views 
depicting the domain architecture of the TycA-M1–TycB-M2 complex in domain

the acceptor-side PCP2 and the C2 domain in the structure of complex A.
